text:
alyssa: Heads up — hf->redwood converter blew up during the new model bring-up. Download seemed to succeed but conversion fails at safetensors load with shard count mismatch.

ben: ugh, which model + hub path?

alyssa: meta/ggml-chat-7b (we're testing a custom fork). Hub path is: https://huggingface.co/our-org/ggml-chat-7b, revision pinned to `main` for now. Error: `safetensors.IndexError: expected 3 shards, found 2` during `safetensors.safe_open` inside `hf_downloader`.

carmen: if the index.json on the repo lists 3 shards but one failed to upload, hf_hub download might return a 206 partial for that file if auth timed out or token lacked read:org?

alyssa: I double-checked — `git lfs` was fine, `hf_hub_list` shows 3 entries. The converter log shows one of the shard downloads returned HTTP 403 for the `.safetensors` file, but the higher-level code swallowed it and moved on.

mira: can you paste the converter error snippet?

alyssa: sure:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/converter/hf_to_redwood.py", line 321, in convert_model
    weights = safetensors.safe_open(shard_path, framework="pt")
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/safetensors/__init__.py", line 98, in safe_open
    raise IndexError(f"index.json lists {expected} shards, found {found}")
IndexError: index.json lists 3 shards, found 2
```

ben: that matches a partial-download case. Two quick checks: 1) was the HF token rotated recently? 2) are we hitting any internal cache/proxy that might block large files?

alyssa: HF token is fine; I retried locally with `HUGGINGFACE_HUB_TOKEN` and it downloads all 3 shards. In CI (converter job) we use the org machine token stored in Vault — I see `403` logs in the job output for one shard.

infra-bot: deploy-cred-rotation: The machine token used by converter-runner was rotated at 2025-03-02T03:12:10Z. Jobs that started before roll applied may see auth failures.

carmen: that explains the 403. But we should hard-fail the downloader if a shard fails instead of letting conversion continue and then error on index mismatch. Also seen another bug: when we do weight key renames later, converter assumes contiguous key prefixes like `model.` and misses keys named `transformer.` — so some layers are left with old keys and runtime fails with KeyError.

alyssa: yep I hit that: after forcing a re-download, the conversion continued but then the conversion runtime raised `KeyError: 'transformer.wte.weight'` in Redwood format loader. The mapping table in `hf_to_redwood/rename_keys.py` only maps `model.embed_tokens` -> `embed_tokens`, not the `transformer` variants.

ben: two separate fixes then: 1) make hf downloader authoritative — on any HTTP != 200 for shard -> abort and surface a clear error thread (401/403/404). 2) expand key-rename mapping to include alternative prefixes and a fuzzy matcher (fallback regex) so we don't miss legacy key names.

mira: also we should respect `revision` pinning: currently converter's `download_repo` call uses `revision=None` which picks whatever default branch is latest; in cases where a user overwrote an index file in-place during an upload, you can end up with index.json pointing to shards that aren’t in that commit. Recommend defaulting to explicit `revision` passed from onboarding metadata.

alyssa: agreed. For immediate unblock I patched the converter in our sandbox: force `revision="refs/heads/main"` (ugh) and add explicit HTTP checks. Worked — full conversion completed and local evals look fine except for a small tokenizer mismatch.

ben: what tokenizer mismatch? special tokens?

alyssa: the HF tokenizer has `<|system|>` as a special token. Our chat template conversion dropped it because `config.json` had `add_special_tokens=true` but converter only reads `special_tokens_map` for known keys. Patch suggestion: read `tokenizer.json`/`tokenizer_config.json` for any `special_tokens_map` and merge keys.

carmen: also remember some repos store tokenizers as `s3://` behind presigned URLs — HF hub will surface those as redirects which break some internal downloaders that don't follow redirects for large files. Another reason to use huggingface_hub's `hf_hub_download` which handles redirects and auth properly.

mira: I'll open two PRs: one to make downloader strict (abort on non-200), fail earlier, and log which file failed and http status; second to extend the rename map and add a small unit test that emulates `transformer.*` keys.

alyssa: please also add an integration test that simulates token rotation mid-download (force a 403 on shard 2) so we don't regress. Maybe reuse the CI local proxy to inject failures.

infra-bot: ticket created: INFRA-1427 (converter: strict shard download + auth failure test).

ben: tiny UX note — when conversion fails we should upload the raw downloaded tarball to our artifacts bucket with a metadata file listing which shards were present and which failed. Saves a lot of debugging back-and-forth.

alyssa: agreed. For now I'll re-run the job with the patched downloader and pinned revision. I'll post results in this thread. Thanks all :thumbsup:

mira: :eyes: ping me if you want a quick pair on the rename regexes.

alyssa: will do.
